Senses.PreferredTarget: mountains, rivers, and the great earth
Senses.Explanation: Literally, mountains, rivers, great, and earth. The expression names the whole visible terrain. Across the allowlisted corpus it occurs 2,224 times in 305 texts. Masters answer with it when asked what lies between heaven and earth and what the appearance of mind is; elsewhere they ask whether it is the same as or different from oneself, say that calling something by this name meets the object while refusing the name turns away from it, and include it with the sun, moon, and stars in what does not go outside one's mind. One later record gives its own local formulation: a portion of unknowing is called mountains, rivers, and the great earth. That formulation is reported as this record's wording, not imposed on the other occurrences.
Senses.Note: The reverse-order variant 'the great earth, mountains, and rivers' is frequent (562 occurrences in 211 texts). The evidence preserves the expression's ordinary collective reference while recording several distinct ways masters deploy it in questions and answers.

Occurrences.Kwic: 塚上草離離。問：上是天，下是地，未審中間是甚麼物？師曰：山河大地。曰：恁麼則謝師答話。師曰：大地山河。曰：和尚何得瞞人？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: An anonymous monk asks a named master what is between heaven and earth; the exchange also immediately reverses the expression's word order.

Occurrences.Kwic: 子閑。蘄州四祖山法演禪師蘄州四祖山法演禪師桂州人。僧問：如何是心相？師曰：山河大地。曰：如何是心體？師曰：汝喚甚麼作山河大
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The passage identifies the master in the text; the name is left unlinked because this occurrence was not assigned a verified roster spelling.

Occurrences.Kwic: 一念昏沉便是無明，無明生起一分有知，謂之眾生；一分無知，謂之山河大地。明暗色空，山河影現，搖動知覺謂之塵，知覺吸攬前塵謂之念
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A small-talk section of this discourse record supplies an explicit local wording for the term.

Occurrences.Kwic: 且放下著。我喚作露柱則觸。不喚作露柱則背。爾又如何奪。我喚作山河大地則觸。不喚作山河大地則背。爾又如何奪。有箇舟峯長老云。某
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The discourse speaker applies the paired 'call it' and 'do not call it' formula first to a pillar and then to the landscape expression.

Occurrences.Kwic: 曰：不知最親切。又同三人舉肇論，至天地與我同根處，藏曰：山河大地與上座自己是同是別？師曰：別。藏竪起兩指，師曰：同。藏又竪
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A two-speaker exchange tests both 'different' and 'same'; null attribution avoids assigning the entire exchange to one speaker.

Occurrences.Kwic: 不可更頭上安頭觜上加觜但莫生異見山是山水是水僧是僧俗是俗山河大地日月星辰揔不出汝心三千世界都來是汝箇自己何處有多般心外無法滿目青
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The governing section is the Wanling record of Huangbo; the roster link is left null pending an exact canonical-name check.

Senses.Explanation: Literally, “East Mountain walks on water.” The phrase occurs 290 times in 131 allowlisted texts. In Yunmen's record it is his answer when a monk asks, “What is the buddhas' place of emergence?” (如何是諸佛出身處). Later records quote it as “Yunmen's saying”, ask directly for its import, set it beside other answers to the same question, and compose verses on it. A lamp biography says the hermit Ru first clarified his own view while examining this saying. Yuanwu later repeats Yunmen's exchange and supplies his own different answer to the same question: “The fragrant wind comes from the south; the halls give rise to a slight coolness” (薰風自南來，殿閣生微涼). The corpus gives no lexical gloss explaining how the mountain walks; this entry therefore retains the sentence Yunmen spoke and reports its recorded deployments.
Senses.Note: This is a portable case-saying rather than an ordinary report about a mountain. East Mountain is translated rather than left as an unexplained place-name. The headword is linked to the broader “place of emergence” entry, but its wording is not treated as a definition of that separate term.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。如何是諸佛出身處。師曰。東山水上行。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yunmen's own record supplies the question and exact answer.

Occurrences.Kwic: 台州天台如庵主久依法真。因看雲門東山水上行語。發明己見。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A lamp biography explicitly calls the phrase Yunmen's saying and records Ru examining it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問雲門：如何是諸佛出身處？門曰：東山水上行。若是天寧即不然，忽有人問：如何是諸佛出身處？只向他道：薰風自南來，殿閣生微涼。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu quotes Yunmen and visibly supplies a different answer to the identical question.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問：東山水上行，意旨如何？師曰：初三十一，不用擇日。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A later public interview makes Yunmen's sentence itself the object of a question.

Occurrences.Kwic: 雲門因僧問如何是諸佛出身處師曰東山水上行。頌曰。東山水上行出處甚分明好看塵沙佛波濤四面生
Occurrences.AttributionNote: A case-and-verse collection preserves the exchange and immediately begins a verse with its answer.

Senses.PreferredTarget: a slip of speech (being caught out / defeated in a dialogue by one's own words)
AlternateTargets: a slip of the tongue that loses the exchange
Senses.Explanation: Literally 'speech-fall' (話 speech + 墮 to fall/drop). Its dominant attested form is a verdict spoken in dialogue -- (話墮也) (164 hits / 58 allowlist files), with second-person forms (汝話墮) (16 / 7), (你話墮) (9 / 5), (爾話墮) (2 / 1), the variant (話墮了也) (32 / 22), and the fixed reply (是汝話墮也) (one exchange, following 如何是好手人, carried in 5 witness files). The one so judged presses back with (什麼處是話墮)/(話墮處) (7 hits / 6 files); the recorded answers to that question are Muzhou's (擔枷過狀萬里崖州自領出去) and Yunmen's (七棒對十三). The word is not reserved to the master's side: monks and commentators say it of a master (和尚話墮也, 6 hits / 6 files -- e.g. X69n1343, where a master raises Yunmen's 話墮也 verdict, asks 爾見什麼處是話墮處, and the monk answers 和尚話墮也); masters say it of themselves (山僧話墮, 2 files; 老僧話墮也。明眼者試辨看, J27nB189), of both parties at once (師曰。彼此話墮, T51n2076), of absent masters (恁麼則趙州話墮。僧便出。師曰：恁麼則山僧話墮, X82n1571; 法眼和尚話墮也不知, X79n1559), and of Bodhidharma (老胡九年話墮。可惜當時放過 -- in Dahui's own record T47n1998A, and 9 hits / 9 files counting retellings); in one exchange the master who declares (爾話墮也) adds (我話亦墮汝作麼生) (one case, 5 witness files). The corpus contains no passage defining the term (no 謂之話墮, 話墮者, or 名為話墮 anywhere in the allowlist); when asked where the slip lies, the masters answer as quoted above. The texts leave (話墮) without gloss, and so does this entry.
Senses.Note: 577 hits across 172 files of the 462-file allowlist (XML tags/notes/rdg stripped, whitespace collapsed, punctuation retained -- all counts in this entry use this convention). The reciprocal uses are two separate cases: (我話亦墮) (the curated Baozi occurrence; one exchange carried in 5 witness files T51n2076, X79n1557, X80n1565, X80n1568, X81n1571) and (彼此話墮) (T51n2076 0401c02: 師問僧。汝念什麼經。曰法華經。師曰。彼此話墮). Curated occurrences span (語錄), (廣錄), (燈錄) and (會元).

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云你為什麼話墮進云什麼處是話墮處師云擔枷過狀萬里崖州自領出去
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Muzhou: (你為什麼話墮) ('why have you slipped?') -- monk: (什麼處是話墮處) ('where is the slip?') -- Muzhou: (擔枷過狀萬里崖州自領出去) ('shoulder the cangue and file your own complaint; take yourself off the ten thousand li to Yazhou').

Occurrences.Kwic: 師云。話墮也。進云。什麼處是話墮。師云。七棒對十三。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: In Yunmen's own Extensive Record: the verdict (話墮也), the monk's (什麼處是話墮) ('where is the slip?'), and the recorded answer (七棒對十三) ('seven blows against thirteen').

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰。爾話墮也。又曰。我話亦墮汝作麼生。僧無對。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Baozi Xiaowu (婺州金鱗報恩院寶資曉悟大師; not in the roster). The master declares (爾話墮也), then adds (我話亦墮汝作麼生) ('my speech has fallen too -- what do you make of it?'); the monk had no reply (僧無對).

Occurrences.Kwic: 老胡九年話墮。可惜當時放過。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui says it of Bodhidharma (老胡, 'the old foreigner') and his nine years facing the wall: 'the old foreigner's nine years -- a speech-fall; a pity it was let pass at the time.' Also in Dahui's own record (老胡九年話墮。可惜當時放過, T47n1998A); 9 hits / 9 files counting retellings.

Occurrences.Kwic: 和尚因甚麼如此。師曰。汝話墮也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The verdict form: the monk asks (和尚因甚麼如此) ('why are you like this?'), and Guichen replies (汝話墮也).

AlternateTargets: to make an interpretation of the saying
to understand it as talk about something
Senses.Explanation: Literally, to understand or construe speech. In Chan records it repeatedly names an auditor's reduction of a reply or case to an explanatory category. Yuanwu reports that people construe Dongshan's 'three pounds of hemp' as an answer based on his work weighing hemp; Dahui says blind fellows construe Zhaozhou's instruction as merely 'wash the bowl'; and Fayan says that for twenty years he construed Jiashan's line only as talk about scenery. The records also expose competing constructions: a collection says people construed Vimalakirti's response as silence, a pause, remaining seated, or not answering, but none reached it. A master can therefore warn, after answering 'what is buddha?', 'do not construe it as answer-buddha talk.' Elsewhere the word is itself put under interview pressure: 'without relying on the three-inch tongue, try to construe it.' The Chan-specific bend is observable and critical: construing the words (話會) is not neutral comprehension but the named act of fitting a live saying into talk about a subject. The entry does not decide what an unexplained saying ultimately means.
Senses.Note: Zen-allowlist count: 745 hits in 224 texts. Definition-formula searches and high-frequency files were reviewed; no distinct referent or word class emerged. Family check: understanding a saying (解會) and intellectual understanding (知解) concern grasping more broadly, while construing the words (話會) specifically keeps the spoken saying or words in view. The answer-buddha, scenery, bowl-washing, competing-construction, and no-tongue deployments are separately anchored.

Occurrences.Kwic: 如何是佛。師曰。卭州多出九節杖。曰謝師指示。師曰。且莫作答佛話會却。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: After answering 'what is buddha?' with 'Qiongzhou produces many nine-jointed staffs,' the master warns: 'do not construe it as answer-buddha talk.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 人多作話會道。洞山是時在庫下。秤麻。有僧問。所以如此答。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Yuanwu reports the common construction that Dongshan answered 'three pounds of hemp' because he was weighing hemp in the storehouse.

Occurrences.Kwic: 而今諸方有一種瞎漢。往往盡作洗鉢盂話會了。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui says blind fellows commonly make Zhaozhou's case merely a 'wash-the-bowl' construction.

Occurrences.Kwic: 後來法眼云我二十年秪作境話會。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Fayan says, 'for twenty years I construed it only as talk about scenery.'

Occurrences.Kwic: 者一轉語，叢林話會不少，有道默然，有道良久，有道據坐，有道不對，要且摸索不著
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The collection inventories several constructions of one turning phrase—silence, a pause, remaining seated, or not answering—and says they still do not reach it.

Occurrences.Kwic: 到這裏不假三寸試話會看。不假耳試釆聽看。不假眼試辯白看。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Interview challenge: 'here, without relying on the three-inch tongue, try to construe it; without ears, try to listen; without eyes, try to distinguish.'

Senses.PreferredTarget: the word or saying raised for investigation
Senses.Explanation: The first graph means speech or a saying (話); the second can mark a head or end and also serves as a noun-forming suffix (頭). In the passages grouped here, the compound names a word, question, or saying that someone is explicitly told to look at, raise, take up, remember, recite, or investigate. Dahui Zonggao says to 'look at a saying' (看箇話頭) and immediately supplies Zhaozhou's question, 'Does a dog have Buddha-nature or not?' (狗子還有佛性也無), answered 'no' (無). The corpus likewise supplies Zhaozhou's cypress tree in the courtyard, Yunmen's dry shit-stick, and other named exchanges after directions to look at a saying. Later records define the term directly. Hanyue Fazang says, 'What is called a saying is one matter or one thing before the eyes' (所謂話頭者，即目前一事一法也), and elsewhere says that this one question gathers all spoken and unspoken words of the worldly and world-transcending, therefore it is called the saying (只者一問，便收盡世出世間一切有言無言等語，故謂之話頭). Ruibai Mingxue says that what is spoken of as the saying is one's own native scenery, distinctly and singly bright, not interrupted by a hair's breadth (所言話頭者，即自己本地風光，歷歷孤明，不可絲毫間斷). A later retrospective reports that only in the Song did talk of looking at sayings and exerting effort arise (直至宋朝，始有看話頭、作工夫之說), and says people were told to take up a saying and look at what principle it was. The Discourse on Forging in the Chan Gate criticizes guarding a dead saying without raising doubt (死守話頭，不起疑情). Current allowlist counts show the range: the headword as 'saying' (話頭), 2,575 hits in 297 texts; 'investigate a saying' (參話頭), 187 in 76; 'look at a saying' (看話頭), 118 in 46; 'one saying' (一句話頭), 136 in 30; 'one's originally investigated saying' (本參話頭), 89 in 50; 'raise a saying' (舉話頭), 35 in 24; 'take up a saying' (提話頭), 32 in 24; 'the saying consisting of the word no' (無字話頭), 14 in 12; and 'dead saying' (死話頭), 40 in 33.
Senses.Note: This is a word or saying in the Chinese record, not the name of a separate object, exercise, mantra, or special category. The sense is corpus-wide even though Dahui is a prominent early source: later masters define and deploy it independently, so historical prominence does not justify a master-specific SenseKey. Hanyue also records the comparison, 'In ancestral-teacher Chan it is called the saying; among Confucians it is called investigating things' (在祖師禪謂之話頭，在儒家謂之格物). Tiemei's record asks separately about the head, tail, and waist of a saying (話頭、話尾、話腰). The corpus has only two hits for 'saying-tail' (話尾) and one for 'saying-waist' (話腰), so those forms are recorded as wordplay rather than general definitions.

Occurrences.Kwic: 只就動止處。看箇話頭。便是釋迦老子達磨大師出來也。只是這箇。僧問趙州。狗子還有佛性也無。州云無。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dahui’s own record. He says to “look at a saying” and immediately gives Zhaozhou’s dog question and the answer “no.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 單單提起箇無義味話頭，自最初一日立定脚頭，不得分毫移動，密密與之做向前去
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Zhongfeng Mingben’s Miscellaneous Records, in his address to the assembly at Shunxin Hermitage. He tells the assembly to take up a saying “without the flavor of meaning” and continue with it from the first day.

Occurrences.Kwic: 所謂話頭者，即目前一事一法也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Hanyue Fazang’s own Extended Record. This is an explicit definition: “What is called a saying is one matter or one thing before the eyes.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 只者一問，便收盡世出世間一切有言無言等語，故謂之話頭。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Hanyue’s second explicit definition: “This one question gathers all spoken and unspoken words of the worldly and world-transcending; therefore it is called the saying.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 在祖師禪謂之話頭，在儒家謂之格物。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Hanyue draws the comparison himself: “In ancestral-teacher Chan it is called the saying; among Confucians it is called investigating things.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 所言話頭者，即自己本地風光，歷歷孤明，不可絲毫間斷。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Ruibai Mingxue’s own record. The sentence explicitly begins “What is spoken of as the saying…” and gives Ruibai’s definition; the entry reports it as his wording rather than a universal gloss.

Occurrences.Kwic: 直至宋朝，始有看話頭、作工夫之說。當時只教人提起箇話頭，看是什麼道理？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Record of Weilin Daopei’s Return to the Mountain gives this later historical retrospective: only in the Song did talk of “looking at the saying” and “doing the work” arise; people were told to take up a saying and look at its principle.

Occurrences.Kwic: 而世有教人死守話頭，不起疑情者，此參禪大病也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Discourse on Forging in the Chan Gate supplies a text-drawn negative contrast: teaching people to guard a dead saying without raising doubt is called a major illness in investigating Chan.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧問：「如何是話頭？」師云：「腳上生腳。」「如何是話尾？」師云：「如牛無角。」「如何是話腰？」師云：「你且行路。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Recorded Sayings of Master Tiemei Sanbazhang preserves an interview asking separately, “What is saying-head?”, “What is saying-tail?”, and “What is saying-waist?” The three answers are retained as an attested wordplay sequence without assigning them a further gloss.

Senses.PreferredTarget: a saying, remark, or turn in an exchange
Senses.Explanation: In encounter records, the same word denotes words spoken in an exchange: a saying, a remark, or the turn being carried by the speakers. Dongshan Liangjie appraises one as “a fine saying; it only lacks a follow-up line” (好箇話頭，只欠進語). Yunmen Xianqin speaks after a long silence and calls it “a fine saying” (好箇話頭), adding that it must not be recited wrongly elsewhere. Yunmen Wenyan asks for “my saying” to be returned (還我話頭來). In the “three pounds of hemp” exchange, Fuyan Liangya says that Dongshan Shouchu supposed Liangya did not understand “his saying” (他這話頭), referring to Dongshan’s answer. Recurrent forms confirm the deployment: “return my saying” (還我話頭來), 78 hits in 44 texts; “does not even recognize the saying” (話頭也不識), 185 hits in 87 texts; “remember the saying” (記得話頭), 68 hits in 61 texts; and “a fine saying” (好箇話頭), 24 hits in 21 texts. The records do not assign one further gloss to all of these conversational uses.
Senses.Note: This sense covers a unit within recorded speech rather than a specified word, question, or saying that someone is told to investigate. It remains lexically connected to the first sense; the split records the distinct constructions and deployments rather than positing two unrelated words.

Occurrences.Kwic: 洞山，山云：好箇話頭，只欠進語。曹云：進甚麼語？洞云：何不問？為甚麼不道？
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dongshan calls the remark “a fine saying” and says it lacks only a follow-up line. The passage then records the requested follow-up.

Occurrences.Kwic: 問。一口吞盡時如何。師曰。我在你肚裏。曰。和尚為甚麼在學人肚裏。師曰。還我話頭來。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Five Lamps Compendium, in Yunmen Wenyan’s section. In a direct exchange, Yunmen answers the follow-up with “Return my saying to me.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂。良久曰。好箇話頭。若到諸方。不得錯舉。便下座。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Five Lamps Compendium, in Yunmen Xianqin’s section. After a long silence, Xianqin says, “A fine saying; if you reach other places, do not recite it wrongly,” and steps down. Xianqin lacks a verified project-roster spelling, so MasterName is null.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧出問。如何是佛。山答曰。麻三斤。參罷。山至寮謂師曰。我今日答這僧話。得麼。曰。恰值某淨髮。山曰。你元來作這去就。拂袖便出。師曰。這老漢將謂我明他這話頭不得。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Five Lamps Compendium, in Fuyan Liangya’s section. Dongshan Shouchu answers “three pounds of hemp”; Liangya later calls that answer “his saying.” Two speakers are present and Liangya lacks a verified project-roster spelling, so MasterName is null.
